# Information-gathering, Solution, and Verification in one script.

# 1) Inspects the input workbook and reports where "Gross Pay" occurs in column D
#    and how many consecutive blank rows are immediately above each occurrence.
# 2) Writes a VBA macro (as plain text) into Sheet1!A1 of the workbook copy saved to output_path.
#    (The instruction requested VB code; placing it into A1 leaves the rest of the sheet intact.)

        types.append(type(v).__name__)
    print(f"Row {r:3d}: values={vals}  types={types}")

# Find occurrences of "Gross Pay" in column D and count blank rows above each occurrence
occurrences = []
for r in range(1, max_row + 1):
    v = ws.cell(row=r, column=4).value  # column D
    if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip() == "Gross Pay":
        # Count consecutive blank rows immediately above row r
        k = r - 1
        blank_count = 0
        while k >= 1:
            row_any = False
            # Consider a row blank if all cells in A..D are None or empty string after stripping
            for c in range(1, max_col + 1):
                cell_val = ws.cell(row=k, column=c).value
                if cell_val is not None and (not (isinstance(cell_val, str) and cell_val.strip() == "")):
                    row_any = True

                break

            k -= 1
        occurrences.append((r, blank_count))
print("\nFound 'Gross Pay' occurrences in column D (row, blank_rows_above):")
for occ in occurrences:
    print(occ)

# Also display a couple of the example spans the instruction mentioned if present:
# (They mentioned rows 29-36 and 70-76 as examples; report whether those ranges are blank and
# whether 'Gross Pay' sits right below them.)
def is_row_blank(row_idx):
    for c in range(1, max_col + 1):
        v = ws.cell(row=row_idx, column=c).value
        if v is not None and not (isinstance(v, str) and v.strip() == ""):
            return False
    return True

for start,end in [(29,36),(70,76)]:
    if end <= max_row:
        range_blank = all(is_row_blank(r) for r in range(start, end+1))
        below_row = end + 1
        below_val = ws.cell(row=below_row, column=4).value if below_row <= max_row else None
        print(f"Rows {start}-{end} all blank? {range_blank}. Cell D{below_row} value: {below_val!r}")

# 2) Solution: write VB code into Sheet1!A1 and save to output_path

# Read workbook again (this time writable). We'll modify only cell A1 in Sheet1.
wb2 = load_workbook(filename=str(input_path))
ws2 = wb2[sheet_name]

vba_code_lines = [
    "Sub DeleteBlankRowsAboveGrossPay()",
    "    ' This macro scans column D for the text ""Gross Pay"".",

    "    Dim ws As Worksheet",
    "    Set ws = ThisWorkbook.Sheets(\"Sheet1\")",

    "                    k = k - 1",
    "                    r = r - 1  ' adjust current position because a row above was removed",
    "                Else",
    "                    Exit Do",
    "                End If",
    "            Loop",
    "        End If",
    "    Next r",
    "End Sub"
]

vba_text = "\n".join(vba_code_lines)

rows_to_check = 384

for r in range(1, rows_to_check + 1):
    for c in range(1, cols_to_check + 1):
        cell = ws_out.cell(row=r, column=c)
        val = cell.value
        # For consistent printing of types, get the Python type name
        tname = type(val).__name__
        # Print coordinate, value repr, and type name
        coord = cell.coordinate
        print(f"{coord}: {val!r} (type: {tname})")

print("\nDone.")
